source.display_title: 06/06/2026 - Jay Bremner x Ben Byrne  — Lost

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced on the call; the prospect self-booked after finding Trevor the same morning — 'Six hours. ... I came across him this morning'.

prospect.name: Jay Bremner
prospect.occupation: General foreman for an HVAC company specialising in hospitals; photographer / content creator as a side hustle
prospect.family_status: No children yet; referenced wanting to pick up and play with future kids
prospect.training_background: Self-described fit and active — calisthenics, pull-up bar, running, trails and mountains; CrossFit and sports in the past; group workouts in Vancouver; has done Spartan-type races and plans a December HYROX; seasonal pattern of dropping off in winter
prospect.medical: Recurring lower back issues and SI joint flare-ups that come and go; back can spasm when pushing heavy weight — 'I'll start getting spasms and stuff like that'; self-describes it as discomfort rather than an injury. Generally inflexible. No diagnosis, clinician or treatment disclosed.

signals: Self-directed and capable — 'I'm a pretty fit and active individual', already runs calisthenics, running and group workouts without help
Explicitly shopping and price-benchmarking — 'obviously, I'm in, I'm shopping around and seeing what's the best fit for me'
Named a substitute he believes is cheaper and adequate — 'I'm pretty sure I could find somebody for cheaper in-person that would meet with me a few times a week that specializes in kettlebells'
Set his own value ceiling rather than accepting the anchor — 'I think that the value for me would be like $6.50 a month, maybe $6.00'
Not the_optimizer: price was a hard barrier, not a quality signal

goals.text: Improve mobility, which he says has never been his strong suit and matters more as he ages
Get leaner and see his abs again
Be as fit as possible by 40 so he can 'tick off my 40s as best I can'
Get genuinely good at kettlebells rather than dabbling — 'I want to be better at kettlebells and I see the benefit of kettlebells specifically'
Have structure and routine so training does not drop off when work gets busy
Be able to pick up and play with future kids in all positions, not just linear movement

pains.text: No structure or routine — 'I lack structure and accountability for sure. I get after it, but I don't have any structure'
Training is the first thing dropped when work gets busy — 'the first thing to go is the thing that I don't have accountability for or structure with'
Annual winter fall-off where he becomes sedentary and gains fat — 'I usually have like a month or two where I'm just like relaxed and putting some fat on'
Recurring back and SI joint flare-ups that spasm when he pushes heavy weight
Poor flexibility and stiffening with age — 'I definitely don't want my body to get stiff'
Eating out more than he wants since returning from six weeks in Peru
Kettlebell technique gaps — 'my still kills my wrist' and 'I haven't mastered the timing yet'

objections.raw_quote: So $8,400 for six months. That's like $1,400 per month. That's significant.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged it as an investment and reframed the programme as knowledge transfer rather than a subscription, then asked how he felt about it. Did not isolate the objection or explore finances.

objections.raw_quote: So, like, I'm pretty sure I could find somebody for cheaper in-person that would meet with me a few times a week that specializes in kettlebells. I can think of a few off my head already, actually.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the point ('there's always cheaper people out there for sure'), then offered to 'find a way to meet in the middle' with less financially committing options rather than defending the differentiated value.

objections.raw_quote: I'd probably be prepared to, let's see. Yeah. I don't know. I think like from the information at hand, I think that the value. For me, would be like $6.50 a month, maybe $6.00 is probably what I would be thinking.
objections.rep_response: Split the offer — described Primal University as the lower-priced tier without accountability, then said 'the price is not negotiable, but we could go from six months down to three', quoting $4,000 for three months.

objections.raw_quote: Unfortunately, that's not something that I think that is a value for that price, I think. It's a bit too much. That's kind of how I feel about the full coaching program. But I like what you guys are doing here, and I definitely see the value of what you're offering. Unfortunately, the asking price is just a bit too much for me, for sure.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the no ('Gosh, man. Well... Fair enough') and pivoted to the $199/month Primal University, dropping a Skool link in the Zoom chat.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: None stated for the coaching programme. For Primal University the rep said 'If you go monthly, it's like pay-as-you-go. So you can cancel at any point. Like, if you join in the first 30 days, not really getting anything out of it, you can just cancel through the app.'

evidence: Explicit refusal of the coaching programme: 'Unfortunately, the asking price is just a bit too much for me, for sure.'
Rejected the improvised three-month tier too: 'Unfortunately, that's not something that I think that is a value for that price.'
No payment taken, no payment link sent, no onboarding scheduled.

Counter-evidence: he did not close the door entirely — he asked for the Primal University landing page ('Share that link with me, so I can just look a little bit deeper into that. I can make an assessment on that'), so a $199/month self-serve sale remains live.
Call ended cordially with no follow-up appointment booked.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review the Primal University Skool link the rep dropped in the Zoom chat and decide on his own; no follow-up call scheduled.

notable.note: The rep improvised a three-month / $4,000 tier live on price pressure — a price that appears nowhere in the stated $6,000/6mo, $9,000/12mo structure — and did so immediately after telling the prospect 'the price is not negotiable'. He also invited negotiation earlier ('we'll see if we can find a way to meet in the middle'). Separately, the prospect disclosed recurring back spasms and SI joint dysfunction that flare when he lifts heavy, and the rep pitched a loaded kettlebell programme without ever asking whether a clinician had looked at it. The prospect had discovered Trevor six hours before the call and was fully unwarmed — no setter, no prior nurture — which is worth noting against the close rate.

quality.notes: Frequent swaps. Long passages are inverted — e.g. the whole programme pitch from 00:03:00 ('Fathom right in with the with the strength and conditioning') is labelled to the prospect but is clearly the prospect's own continued turn, and the block at 00:24:00-00:25:00 comparing HYROX linearity is split across both labels mid-sentence. Roles were resolved from content throughout. Prospect's speaker label is 'Jaybre Photo', not his name. Numbers are mangled by the transcription: weight rendered '1160, bet, or just under' (read as ~160 lb), Primal University pricing rendered '$1.99 per month' and '$19.99 for the year' (read as $199/mo and $1,999/yr, consistent with the stated ~$350 saving), and his value ceiling rendered '$6.50 a month, maybe $6.00' (read as $650/$600 per month).
